Question B-007-004-002.

Why the correct answer is right: Daytime D-region ionization absorbs low-frequency sky-wave energy, so distant stations on those low bands may disappear until the lower region weakens.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "The presence of ionized clouds in the E region": The presence of ionized clouds in the E region points to the wrong region and an imprecise mechanism.
- sourceIndex 2: "The splitting of the F region into two sub-regions": The splitting of the F region into two sub-regions can affect HF propagation, but it is not the reason low-frequency distant stations vanish in daylight.
- sourceIndex 3: "The weather below the ionosphere": The weather below the ionosphere can affect VHF/UHF tropospheric paths, not the main daytime loss of distant low-frequency sky wave.
